title: If you don't run your own LLM proxy, how do you know whats going on?
summary: This article discusses the importance of running your own LLM proxy layer for observability and control when integrating LLMs into applications. Without a proxy, developers lack visibility into API calls, responses, latency, errors, and costs. The author argues that a self-hosted proxy is essential for debugging, monitoring, and understanding what's happening with your AI integrations.
problem_solved: Lack of visibility and control over LLM API interactions, making debugging and monitoring AI applications difficult.
why_valuable: A proxy layer enables observability, cost tracking, request logging, and better control over LLM behavior in production environments.
